label: GO step near episode end (low value) when choosing a2
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (97% of mass), only in the last ~10 trials of the episode (trials 90-99 hold 99.7% of mass, nothing before trial 80), and only when the agent is about to choose a2 (model_act==2 holds 96% of mass, a1 almost never). In the profile, the value head output being in its lowest bin (<5.22) captures 100% of the mass; that reflects the shrinking remaining-episode return, so the unit is an end-of-episode timer gated by an a2 choice. Recorded with value<4 and policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) < -3. Both are the model own outputs, so no FUTURE variable is used; ep_trial>=93 & choice<-3 gives similar F1 (0.73). Magnitude grows over the episode tail (activation goes up across successive trials of a window) and with strong, repeated a2 preference after rewarded a2 trials. Weak activations at D1/D2 are rare. It does not fire at a1 choices, before trial ~85, or on any rewarded-input step (in_rew==1). False positives are mostly a2 GO steps that follow unrewarded or rare trials, where the a2 preference is weaker.

issues: Most factual claims check out on dev: GO holds 96.9% of mass; trials 90-99 hold 99.7% and the unit never fires before trial 80; value < 5.22 holds 100%; model_act==2 holds 95.9%; dev P0.800 R0.747 F0.773 M0.917, and ep_trial>=93 & choice<-3 scores F0.732. On test the original predicate scores P0.771 R0.733 F0.752 M0.896.

The false positives form one systematic class, not noise. They are GO steps after an UNREWARDED previous trial. Splitting the predicate by prev_reward: with prev_reward==1 it has dev P0.960 (test P0.936); with prev_reward==0 it has dev P0.518 (test P0.509), i.e. about half of its firings there are wrong. The misses output shows the same thing: nearly every false-positive window has r0 at that trial's D1. The explanation mentions this ('after unrewarded or rare trials') but files it under weaker a2 preference. In fact choice is already below -3 on those steps, so the predicate does not capture this effect.

The cause is the value threshold, which depends on the previous reward. After a reward the unit fires up to value of about 4.3. After no reward it needs value below about 3.5. A single value<4 cut is too strict after rewarded trials (misses there) and too loose after unrewarded ones (false positives).

The claim 'does not fire on any step with reward input 1' is true only trivially, because in_rew is nonzero only at D1, where the unit rarely fires anyway. It is also misleading: 81% of the activation mass falls on trials whose previous trial WAS rewarded (prev_reward==1), at the GO step that follows.

The label overclaims a little: 'near episode end' is a proxy. The value-head output is the tighter variable (ep_trial>=93 is worse, F0.732), so 'low value' should come first. The bottom activation quartile is only 26% covered, consistent with the threshold being wrong after rewarded trials.

The better predicate uses only observed or model-internal variables (prev_reward is the D1 reward input; value and choice are model outputs). It improves test F1 from 0.752 to 0.844 and mass recall from 0.896 to 0.939, so the original predicate leaves a correctable systematic gap.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step with a strong a2 preference when the model's value estimate is very low (last ~10 trials of the episode); the value cutoff is higher after a rewarded previous trial (~4.3) than after an unrewarded one (~3.5)
